## The vulnerability (CWE-88, argument injection)

`--base` / `--head` / the `commit` revision reached a `git` argv unvalidated.
`internal/cli/root.go:748` and `:754` assigned `rest[i]` straight to `parsed.base` /
`parsed.head`; the leading-dash guard at `:756` only covered the sibling *path* branch.
`runCommit` took its revision positionally at `:655` with no check.

Git parses options anywhere ahead of `--`, so a value beginning with `-` stops being a
revision and becomes a **flag of the git command it lands in** — `gitutil.ChangedFiles`'
`git diff -z --name-status --find-renames <base> <head> --`, `gitutil.FirstParent`'s
`git rev-parse <rev>^`, `gitutil.ShowFile`'s `git show <rev>^{tree}:<path>`.

Arbitrary file overwrite outside the repository, exit code 0. Reproduced on `cceb4de`:

```
$ printf 'TOP SECRET PRIVATE KEY MATERIAL\n' > victim.txt
$ entire-graph diff --repo . --base "--output=$PWD/victim.txt" --head HEAD
Semantic changes --output=/.../victim.txt..HEAD

No semantic entity changes detected.
exit=0
$ xxd victim.txt
00000000: 4d00 612e 676f 00                        M.a.go.
```

`entire graph commit '--output=/path/victim'` reaches the same argv — `git rev-parse
'--output=/path/victim^'` does not fail first, so `FirstParent` lets the value through.

This is reachable from automation, not only a hostile local shell: the shipped runner
template `.entire/runners/trail-semantic-diff.json` passes a branch-derived value as the
value of `--base`, and its own prompt text calls those branch names untrusted. (That
template prefixes the branch with `origin/`, which incidentally defeats a leading dash
today — which is exactly why the guard belongs at the boundary rather than in one caller.)

## The fix

`validateRevision` (`internal/cli/root.go:719`) refuses an empty revision, one beginning
with `-`, and one containing a NUL, at the CLI boundary. `diff`, `analyze` and `commit` all
route their revisions through it.

This is the guard `internal/gitutil/git.go` **already** applies to the values it splices
into git argv itself — `GrepTreeMatches:168`, `grepTreePaths:237`, `FileCochanges:419` each
reject a leading `-` and an embedded NUL the same way. This change makes the CLI boundary
consistent with them.

Nothing legitimate is refused. A Git revision never begins with `-`, and even the bare `-`
this parser accepts as a *path* is not one — `git diff -` is itself `error: invalid option:
-` (verified, git 2.54.0).

## Failing-first proof

Both tests **compile against the unpatched `origin/main` file and fail at run time**, not
merely at build time. Restoring `internal/cli/root.go` from `origin/main` and keeping the
tests:

```
--- FAIL: TestParseDiffFlagsRejectsOptionShapedRevision (0.00s)
    root_test.go:1105: parseDiffFlags(["--base" "--output=/tmp/entire-graph-victim" "--head" "HEAD"]) accepted an option-shaped revision, want an error
    root_test.go:1105: parseDiffFlags(["--base" "HEAD~1" "--head" "--output=/tmp/entire-graph-victim"]) accepted an option-shaped revision, want an error
    root_test.go:1105: parseDiffFlags(["--base" "-"]) accepted an option-shaped revision, want an error
    root_test.go:1105: parseDiffFlags(["--head" ""]) accepted an option-shaped revision, want an error
--- FAIL: TestOptionShapedRevisionCannotWriteFiles (0.11s)
    --- FAIL: TestOptionShapedRevisionCannotWriteFiles/diff_--base (0.01s)
        root_test.go:1150: diff --base accepted an option-shaped revision
        root_test.go:1159: diff --base let git rewrite a file outside the repository; victim now holds ""
    --- FAIL: TestOptionShapedRevisionCannotWriteFiles/diff_--head (0.01s)
        root_test.go:1159: diff --head let git rewrite a file outside the repository; victim now holds "M\x00a.go\x00"
    --- FAIL: TestOptionShapedRevisionCannotWriteFiles/analyze_--base (0.01s)
        root_test.go:1159: analyze --base let git rewrite a file outside the repository; victim now holds ""
    --- FAIL: TestOptionShapedRevisionCannotWriteFiles/commit_revision (0.01s)
        root_test.go:1159: commit revision let git rewrite a file outside the repository; victim now holds ""
FAIL	github.com/entireio/entire-graph/internal/cli	1.366s
```

With the fix, the same exploit exits 1 and leaves the file untouched:

```
--base "--output=/.../victim.txt" is not a revision: a revision cannot begin with "-", which Git would read as an option
  exit=1  victim=[TOP SECRET PRIVATE KEY MATERIAL]
```

`TestDiffAcceptsOrdinaryRevisions` is the over-rejection guard: `HEAD`, `HEAD~1`, a branch
name, an abbreviated sha, a full sha and an **annotated tag** all still resolve.

The fixtures use ordinary temp-dir paths only — no symlink, device file, exotic filename or
path-separator assumption — so nothing here is platform-specific.

## Gate

`gofmt -l .` empty · `go vet ./...` clean · `go build ./...` clean · `go test ./...` green
(`internal/cli` 5.4s).

## Not done here (needs a file I do not own)

The stronger form of this fix -- resolving each revision through `git rev-parse --verify
--end-of-options <rev>` and passing the resolved OID downstream -- needs a new function in
`internal/gitutil/git.go`, which is outside this PR's scope.

The existing `gitutil.RevParse` is not a substitute for it. It runs plain `git rev-parse
<rev>`, which **exits 0 and echoes the argument straight back** when the value names an
existing path rather than a revision, so a resolution step built on it would pass
non-revisions through silently. Verified on git 2.54.0:

```
$ git rev-parse docs/a.txt          # plain
docs/a.txt
exit=0
$ git rev-parse --verify docs/a.txt # --verify
fatal: Needed a single revision
exit=128
```

Resolving would also change user-visible `Result.Base` / `Result.Head` from `main` / `HEAD`
to a pair of OIDs in both the text header (`internal/sem/text.go:14`) and the JSON payload
(`internal/sem/model.go:84`) -- a behavior change beyond the security fix.

The boundary guard in this PR closes the injection on its own; the OID resolution is
hardening left for the `gitutil` owner.

Here's the review. One check (full race suite) is still running; everything else is done.

## Verdict: **Advisory** — safe to merge, but the PR describes a vulnerability that no longer exists

The code is correct, well-scoped, and worth landing as defense-in-depth. But its central claim was overtaken by **PR 127**, which merged this morning, and the PR body has not caught up.

---

## Findings

### 1. **Advisory (high impact on framing)** — The vulnerability was already fixed by PR 127; this is now defense-in-depth, not a fix

The body claims arbitrary file overwrite outside the repo at exit 0. **It does not reproduce on current main.** I built `2bced5fc` and ran all three vectors against a victim file:

| Vector | main `2bced5fc` (no PR) | PR head |
|---|---|---|
| `diff --base "--output=$V"` | exit 1, **victim intact** | exit 1, victim intact |
| `diff --head "--output=$V"` | exit 1, **victim intact** | exit 1, victim intact |
| `commit "--output=$V"` | exit 1, **victim intact** | exit 1, victim intact |

Cause: `5f1803d8` — *"fix(gitutil,sem): guard rev-parse against option-shaped revisions"* — which is **PR 127's head**. Main now resolves every revision through `git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options` (`internal/gitutil/git.go:101,128`).

That is precisely what this PR's *"Not done here (needs a file I do not own)"* section describes as the stronger fix left for the `gitutil` owner. It got done. So the body's exploit transcript, the "reachable from automation" argument, and the "not done here" section are all stale.

**Correction:** reframe as boundary hardening. It still earns its place — the guard is independent of `gitutil`, and any future call path that doesn't route through `RevParseVerify` is covered.

### 2. **Advisory** — `TestOptionShapedRevisionCannotWriteFiles` no longer discriminates

Reverting *only* `internal/cli/root.go` to main's version on the merged tree, keeping the tests:

```
--- FAIL: TestParseDiffFlagsRejectsOptionShapedRevision   <- still discriminates
--- PASS: TestOptionShapedRevisionCannotWriteFiles         <- all 4 subtests pass WITHOUT the fix
    --- PASS: /diff_--base   --- PASS: /diff_--head
    --- PASS: /analyze_--base --- PASS: /commit_revision
--- PASS: TestDiffAcceptsOrdinaryRevisions                 <- over-rejection guard, correct
```

The headline end-to-end security test is now vacuous with respect to this change — `gitutil` blocks the write either way. Unlike PR 126 nothing is *broken*; the unit test `TestParseDiffFlagsRejectsOptionShapedRevision` still genuinely guards the boundary. But the body presents the e2e test's failure output as the proof, and that proof no longer holds.

**Correction:** keep the test (it guards against `gitutil`'s protection regressing), but note in the body that it now passes on unpatched main, and let the parse-level test carry the failing-first claim.

### 3. **Low** — Test fixture is fragile against global `commit.gpgsign`

`internal/cli/root_test.go:1430` `twoCommitRepo` sets `user.name`/`user.email` and an explicit `init -b`, but not signing. Reproduced:

```console
$ GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=<commit.gpgsign=true, no key> go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'TestOptionShaped...|TestDiffAccepts...'
root_test.go:1409: git [commit -m one]: exit status 128
    fatal: cannot exec '/nonexistent/gpg': No such file or directory
FAIL
```

This is the **same class** as the finding already raised and fixed on this trail (`init.defaultBranch`), and the repo has an established convention — 10+ fixtures in `internal/gitutil`, `internal/sem`, and `cmd/entire-graph` set `commit.gpgsign=false`. In fairness, coverage isn't universal (baseline `internal/gitutil` also fails under that config), so this isn't a regression the PR introduces. One line: `git(t, repo, "config", "commit.gpgsign", "false")`.

---

## Walkthrough

`entire graph diff` reports exactly three semantic changes in `root.go`: `validateRevision` **added** (2 dependents), `parseDiffFlags` and `runCommit` **body_changed** — no signature changes.

`validateRevision(name, rev)` rejects empty, leading-`-`, and embedded-NUL, wired into `--base`, `--head` (`root.go:815,824`) and `commit` (`:692`). `analyze` inherits via `runAnalyze → runDiff`.

**Coverage is complete.** I enumerated every revision entry point on current main: the `--head` in `search`/`def`/`impact`/`neighbors`/`index` is a **boolean** (`flags.Worktree = false`), not a revision; `stats --since` never reaches git argv; and `checkpoint` concatenates into `--grep=Entire-Checkpoint: <id>`, so a leading dash cannot start an argv element. `diff`/`analyze`/`commit` are the whole set.

**No over-rejection.** `runCommit` defaults `rev := "HEAD"`, so bare `commit` is unaffected; no legitimate git revision begins with `-`, and `TestDiffAcceptsOrdinaryRevisions` covers HEAD, `HEAD~1`, branch, abbreviated sha, full sha, and an annotated tag.

**What it actually buys today** is error quality at the boundary:

| input | main | PR head |
|---|---|---|
| `--base "--output=…"` | `resolve diff base "…": git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options …: fatal: …` | `--base "…" is not a revision: a revision cannot begin with "-", which Git would read as an option` |
| `--head ""` | `resolve diff head "": git rev-parse … : fatal: Needed a single revision` | `--head requires a revision` |

## Verification matrix

darwin/amd64, go1.26.5. "Merged" = PR head merged onto `2bced5fc` (clean, no conflicts).

| Command | Tree | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Exploit repro, 3 vectors | main `2bced5fc` | ✅ already blocked — **finding 1** |
| Exploit repro, 3 vectors | PR head | ✅ blocked |
| `gofmt -s -l .` / `go vet ./...` / `go build ./...` | merged | ✅ clean / 0 / ok |
| 3 PR tests | merged | ✅ PASS |
| 3 PR tests, fix reverted | merged | ⚠️ 1 fails, e2e passes — **finding 2** |
| `go test ./internal/cli` (full pkg) | merged | ✅ ok (66.5s) |
| PR tests under global `gpgsign=true` | merged | ❌ FAIL — **finding 3** |
| Skips / build tags / `GOOS` in new tests | merged | ✅ none — runs everywhere |
| `go test -race ./...` | merged | ⏳ running |

## State

- **main:** `2bced5fc` (fast-forwarded; PR 126's merge). Working tree clean.
- **PR 133:** head `85e8c86a`, branch `security/validate-diff-revs`, base `main`, merge-base `11d001d` — **169 behind, 4 ahead**, not draft, `MERGEABLE`/`UNSTABLE`, no reviews. Merges cleanly.
- **CI:** all 10 GitHub checks green **against this exact head**, but run 2026-08-22, before PR 126 and 127 landed. Entire Gates red on approvals only.
- **Trail 93:** 1 finding, low, **resolved** — the `init.defaultBranch` fixture issue, genuinely fixed by `85e8c86a` (`git init -b twocommitrepo-trunk`). Finding 3 is the same class, unraised.

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/93
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## What this is now

**Boundary hardening, not a live vulnerability fix.** When this PR was opened the injection it
describes was exploitable on `main`. It is not any more: #127 (`5f1803d8`, merged 2026-08-23) routed
every revision through `git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options` in `internal/gitutil/git.go`, which
closes the same CWE-88 one layer down. That is precisely the work this PR's original description
deferred as *"needs a file I do not own"* — it got done independently.

This PR still earns its place, for reasons that do not depend on the exploit:

- The guard is at the **CLI boundary** and independent of `gitutil`. Any future call path that
  splices a revision into a git argv without going through `RevParseVerify` is covered by it.
- It turns a leaked-plumbing diagnostic into an explanation. Same input, before and after:

  | input | `main` today | with this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | `--base "--output=FILE"` | `resolve diff base "--output=FILE": git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options --output=FILE: fatal: ...` | `--base "--output=FILE" is not a revision: a revision cannot begin with "-", which Git would read as an option` |
  | `--head ""` | `resolve diff head "": git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options : fatal: Needed a single revision` | `--head requires a revision` |

The original exploit transcript has been removed from this description rather than left standing,
because it no longer reproduces and a reader would waste time trying.

## The original vulnerability (now closed upstream)

`--base` / `--head` / the `commit` revision reached a `git` argv unvalidated. `parseDiffFlags`
assigned `rest[i]` straight to `parsed.base` / `parsed.head`; the leading-dash guard only covered the
sibling *path* branch. `runCommit` took its revision positionally with no check.

Git parses options anywhere ahead of `--`, so a value beginning with `-` stopped being a revision and

content.text: The tag is created in the test but inherits the fixture's repo-level config, so the fix belongs in `twoCommitRepo`. Sweep shows `init`, `config`, `add`, `commit`, `branch`, `tag` — only `commit` and `tag` have signing. Fixing both:

input.command:
SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-thomi-Projects-entire-graph/2a557a2a-c9ee-425b-99d7-537a8e69f87d/scratchpad
cd "$SP/pr133-merge"
python3 - <<'PY'
p="internal/cli/root_test.go"
s=open(p).read()
old = '''	// A developer's global commit.gpgsign would otherwise fail these commits
	// with "gpg failed to sign the data", the same class of global-config
	// dependence as the init.defaultBranch collision above. Most fixtures in
	// this repository already pin it.
	git(t, repo, "config", "commit.gpgsign", "false")'''
new = '''	// A developer's global signing config would otherwise fail this fixture with
	// "gpg failed to sign the data", the same class of global-config dependence
	// as the init.defaultBranch collision above. Both keys are needed and they
	// are independent: commit.gpgsign covers the two commits below, and
	// tag.gpgSign covers the annotated tag TestDiffAcceptsOrdinaryRevisions
	// creates in this repository ("git tag -a" signs under its own key, so
	// pinning only commit.gpgsign still aborts with "unable to sign the tag").
	git(t, repo, "config", "commit.gpgsign", "false")
	git(t, repo, "config", "tag.gpgSign", "false")'''
assert old in s, "anchor not found"
open(p,"w").write(s.replace(old,new,1))
print("patched")
PY
gofmt -l internal/cli/ | head; echo "(gofmt clean)"
echo
echo "=== verify against all three hostile configs ==="
cat > "$SP/fakehome/gitconfig-both" <<'EOF'
[commit]
	gpgsign = true
[tag]
	gpgSign = true
[user]
	signingkey = DEADBEEFNOSUCHKEY
[gpg]
	program = /nonexistent/gpg
EOF
for cfg in gitconfig gitconfig-tag gitconfig-both; do
  printf '  %-18s : ' "$cfg"
  GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL="$SP/fakehome/$cfg" GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null \
    go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'TestDiffAcceptsOrdinaryRevisions|TestOptionShapedRevisionCannotWriteFiles|TestParseDiffFlagsRejectsOptionShapedRevision' -count=1 2>&1 | tail -1
done
printf '  %-18s : ' "normal config"
go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'TestDiffAcceptsOrdinaryRevisions|TestOptionShapedRevisionCannotWriteFiles|TestParseDiffFlagsRejectsOptionShapedRevision' -count=1 2>&1 | tail -1
